clue.text: Urchin throws duffer into river again

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for river on maps

indicators.note: into tells us one piece goes inside the word for again

parts.note: taken as written
a muff is a clumsy bungler, a duffer

explanation.surface: A street kid hurls an incompetent into the river once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' signals the container; 'throws' only makes the surface, since a duffer throwing things is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragged, unkempt child of the streets is called an urchin, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Take a look around — behold king, for a start

parts.note: R is short for Rex, Latin for king
ecce is Latin for behold, as in Ecce Homo

explanation.surface: Have a look about: see, the king goes first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a start' puts R before ECCE. A recce is British informal for a reconnaissance.
explanation.definitionFit: A reconnaissance is a scouting survey of an area, informally shortened.

clue.text: Disheartened girl, loving and elegant

indicators.note: Disheartened means the word girl loses its heart, keeping only its first and last letters

parts.note: amorous means loving, romantic

explanation.surface: A dejected young woman, affectionate and refined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disheartened' removes IR from GIRL, leaving GL. 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamour means alluring, stylish beauty, so the adjective is close to chic or stylish.

clue.text: Decide to change denims, with lipstick on?

parts.note: lipstick is a kind of make-up
taken as written

indicators.note: change tells us to rearrange the letters of denims

explanation.surface: Should one alter one's jeans when wearing lipstick?
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' gives ESMIND; the surface makes 'Decide to change' look like one phrase, but 'to' only links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming to a firm decision is the idiom of settling one's thoughts.

clue.text: Passionate female takes opening without hesitation

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation
a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: A woman seizes the opportunity without pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: F, ER and VENT simply run in order; 'takes' and 'without' only join them, though 'without hesitation' reads as one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent and intensely felt, as a heartfelt plea is.

clue.text: Sloth finds tree, settling in in time

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: settling in says the tree comes to rest inside the word for time

parts.note: an era is a period of time
ti is a palm-like tree of the Pacific, the cabbage tree

explanation.surface: A lazy animal finds a tree and settles in for some time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settling in' marks the container; the first 'in' belongs to it, the second gives letters. Sloth here is idleness, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth as a vice is laziness; this word is the physicist's term for resisting motion, used of torpor.

clue.text: Obstruction, say, for the alliance

indicators.note: say signals that the word for obstruction is spoken, and we write what it sounds like

parts.note: a block is an obstruction or blockage

explanation.surface: A barrier, for example, raised on behalf of a coalition.
explanation.walkthrough: BLOCK, spoken, gives BLOC; 'the' and 'for' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of nations or parties united for common purpose forms a political grouping of this kind.

clue.text: Stars quietly leaving, initially, for lake

indicators.note: leaving, initially says the musical letter for quietly departs from the front of the stars

parts.note: the Plough is the British name for the Big Dipper constellation
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Stars softly depart, at first, from above a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving, initially' drops the P from PLOUGH. A lough is an Irish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: In Ireland, the word for a lake or sea inlet, the Irish counterpart of the Scottish loch.

clue.text: Animal given a month on a new vessel

parts.note: a cat is an animal
Mar is short for March

explanation.surface: A creature gets a month's voyage on a brand-new boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' and 'on' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin-hulled sailing boat is a type of craft or ship.

clue.text: Alter attitude and revise original composition

definitions.meaning: to adopt a different opinion or manner
literally, to rewrite a melody one wrote oneself

explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions: the idiom for changing your views, and its literal sense of altering your own melody.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means adopting a different opinion; literally it is rewriting a melody of one's own.

clue.text: Splendid person, but almost crazy

indicators.note: almost means the word for crazy loses its final letter

parts.note: crackers is British slang for mad or crazy

explanation.surface: Someone is wonderful, yet nearly out of their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last S of CRACKERS. A 'cracker' is British informal for an excellent person or thing.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal usage praises a terrific individual as a real corker or smasher, which this word also means.

clue.text: Thoroughly discuss noxious gases encountered on the way

definitions.meaning: to treat a topic so fully that nothing is left to say

definitions.text: noxious gases encountered on the way
definitions.meaning: fumes from car tailpipes met on the road

explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions: the verb (talk a subject out completely) and the fumes from vehicles on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Covering a subject completely drains it; vehicle fumes pumped from tailpipes are the other sense.

clue.text: Return badly behaved mule to men

indicators.note: badly behaved suggests the letters of mule to men misbehave and fall out of order

explanation.surface: A naughty mule is sent back to its human owners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly behaved' rearranges MULE TO MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Return in the sense of income or earnings from work equals a salary or fee.

clue.text: Book revealing human error

indicators.note: error suggests the letters of human are set down wrongly, out of order

explanation.surface: A volume exposes a mistake made by people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'error' rearranges HUMAN; 'revealing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the minor prophets of the Old Testament, so a book of the Bible.

clue.text: Returned work, including stolen picture

indicators.note: including means the reversed piece holds another word inside it
Returned means the word for work is read backwards

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: A piece of work sent back contained a pirated image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned' gives PO and 'including' marks the container; 'hot' for stolen is slang for goods freshly taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot taken with a camera is an image, the everyday short form for photograph.

clue.text: Successful candidates going through — will they stop at nothing?

parts.note: those who pass an exam are passers
by means via, going through a place

explanation.surface: Exam winners pass through: is there nothing they won't do?
explanation.walkthrough: 'stop at nothing' usually means ruthless; here it means people walking by do not stop at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrians walking past a scene keep going without halting, so the cryptic question describes them.

clue.text: Salesman's description of Stevenson or his donkey

definitions.text: Salesman's description of Stevenson or his donkey

parts.words: Salesman's description of Stevenson or his donkey
parts.note: a commercial rep's job title, and also what Robert Louis Stevenson and his donkey Modestine were on their journey in the Cevennes

explanation.walkthrough: Stevenson wrote 'Travels with a Donkey in the Cevennes'; a salesman on the road is a commercial one too.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a sales rep on the road and someone on a journey are wayfarers in this sense.

clue.text: Aunt Della's ordered carriage

indicators.note: ordered says the letters of aunt della are put into a new order

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter

explanation.surface: An aunt has commissioned a horse-drawn vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges AUNT DELLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A small four-wheeled horse-drawn coach with a folding roof is a type of carriage.

clue.text: South American painting's first completed for hanging

parts.note: US means American, as in US troops

indicators.note: first means take only the opening letter of painting's

parts.note: ended means finished, completed

explanation.surface: A Latin American artwork, its first stage done, is ready to be hung.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American' looks like one idea, but splits into S and US. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hanging from a hook is dangling, held up from above.

clue.text: He may make the Channel and land in an emergency

definitions.text: He may make the Channel and land in an emergency

parts.words: He may make the Channel and land in an emergency
parts.note: a digger of trenches or channels, and also a pilot who brings a plane down on water in an emergency

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a pilot crossing the English Channel; one who digs channels, or puts a plane down on the sea, fits both.
explanation.definitionFit: One who digs trenches is a digger of ditches; to ditch also means to land an aircraft on water.

clue.text: A bold stroke for one on the fiddle

definitions.text: A bold stroke for one on the fiddle

parts.words: A bold stroke for one on the fiddle
parts.note: a daring move by a swindler, or literally a bowing stroke played by a violinist

explanation.walkthrough: 'on the fiddle' suggests cheating, but it means playing the violin; the stroke is a bow movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Violinists draw the bow from frog to tip in this stroke, a basic bowing direction.

clue.text: Materially that's, oddly, always new

parts.note: a dress fabric (materially) whose odd-numbered letters are all N, the abbreviation for new

explanation.walkthrough: Ninon is a sheer silk or voile fabric; its first, third and fifth letters are each N, the abbreviation for new.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a lightweight sheer dress fabric, a material in the literal sense.

clue.text: Keeps omitting to take in this southern town

indicators.note: to take in tells us the answer is held within the words keeps omitting

explanation.surface: Someone keeps forgetting to include a southern town on their route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take in' reveals the town inside keEPS OMitting. Epsom is a Surrey town famous for its racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a market town in Surrey, south of London, home of the Derby.

clue.text: Crude dwelling in Holyhead consumed by fire

indicators.note: consumed by says one letter is swallowed up inside the word for fire

parts.note: to sack is to fire someone from a job
read as holy head: the head, or first letter, of holy

explanation.surface: A rough hut in Holyhead burnt down.
explanation.walkthrough: Holyhead is a Welsh port, but read as 'holy head' it gives H; 'consumed by' puts H inside SACK.
explanation.definitionFit: A roughly built hut or shanty is a basic home.

clue.text: Painting by Wright of Derby, say?

definitions.text: Painting by Wright of Derby, say?

parts.words: Painting by Wright of Derby, say?
parts.note: Joseph Wright of Derby was an 18th-century painter, but read differently a picture of the urban scene of Derby itself

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a work by the painter; the cryptic reading is any picture of a town like Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture of urban buildings and streets is a view of a town, as a landscape is of land.

clue.text: One is stirred up to make dye

indicators.note: stirred up suggests the letters of one is are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is agitated into making colouring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirred up' rearranges ONE IS.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a red fluorescent stain used in microscopy, a colouring agent.

clue.text: Dependable way to prevent leaks

definitions.meaning: loyal and reliable, as a firm supporter is
to stop a flow of liquid, especially blood

explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions: an adjective (loyal, reliable) and a verb (to stem a flow); 'way to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A loyal supporter is steadfast; stemming a flow of blood or water is the verb sense.

clue.text: Bijoux originally usable, somehow, as trinkets

indicators.note: originally means take only the first letter of Bijoux
somehow suggests the letters of usable are rearranged in some unstated way

explanation.surface: Jewels, first of all practical, somehow end up as baubles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' gives AUBLES; the hyphen is just the printed line break in 'somehow'.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy but cheap ornaments are knick-knacks or gewgaws.

clue.text: Bond's all right in the old environment

indicators.note: in, with environment, says one piece sits within the surroundings of another
environment, the surroundings, says the old word for the encloses the other piece

parts.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Agent 007 is perfectly fine in an old-fashioned setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ... environment' marks the container. The 's of Bond's stands for 'is', and the surface's 007 is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden crossbar binding two oxen is a tie or link, as is any bond.

clue.text: Intimidated bishop overcome after argument

indicators.note: after says the word for overcome comes second, following the word for argument

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a row is a quarrel or argument
beaten means defeated, overcome

explanation.surface: A cleric was bullied, defeated after a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intimidated' could look like part of the wordplay, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cowed by bullying and threats has been frightened into submission.
